hook: One mountain in Bolivia paid for an entire empire, and its king still went broke four times.
title: This Mountain Paid for an Empire, and the King Still Went Broke
desc:
Cerro Rico in Potosi produced a huge share of the world's silver for two centuries. Spain's king owned it and still went bankrupt four times. How?
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: The experts told Columbus his maths was wrong. They were right.
title: Columbus Was Wrong About the World, and It Worked Anyway
desc:
Columbus thought the world was much smaller than it is. The experts said no, Portugal said no, and Spain said yes. He should have died at sea.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: Columbus landed in the Bahamas, thought he was in India, and the wrong name stuck for 500 years.
title: Why Native Americans Were Called 'Indians'
desc:
In 1492 Columbus reached an island in the Bahamas and was sure he was near India. The name he gave its people stuck for five centuries.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: In 1494 two kingdoms split the entire world in half with one line on a map.
title: Spain and Portugal Split the World in Half
desc:
The Treaty of Tordesillas drew a line down the Atlantic. Everything west went to Spain, everything east to Portugal. Nobody asked the people living there.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: Cortes landed in Mexico with 500 men, then sank his own ships so nobody could go home.
title: He Sank His Own Ships So Nobody Could Run
desc:
In 1519 Hernan Cortes landed in Mexico with about 500 men and scuttled his fleet. From then on it was win or die.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: 500 Spaniards did not beat the Aztecs alone. Their secret was an interpreter and tens of thousands of allies.
kicker: THE REAL REASON THE AZTECS FELL
title: How 500 Men Toppled the Aztec Empire
desc:
Cortes had two weapons the textbooks skip: Malintzin, his interpreter, and tens of thousands of Tlaxcalan allies who hated Aztec rule.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: The Spanish fled the Aztec capital so loaded with gold that some of them drowned in the canals.
title: They Drowned Because They Carried Too Much Gold
desc:
In 1520 the Aztec capital rose up. The Spanish fled at night, so weighed down with gold that some sank in the canals. They called it La Noche Triste.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: The deadliest weapon the Spanish brought to Mexico was invisible.
title: The Invisible Weapon That Destroyed the Aztecs
desc:
The people of the Americas had never met smallpox. It killed a huge part of Tenochtitlan, including the new emperor, before the final siege.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: The Inca emperor filled a room with gold to buy his freedom. They killed him anyway.
title: He Paid a Room Full of Gold and They Killed Him Anyway
desc:
In 1532 about 170 Spaniards captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca. He paid the greatest ransom in history. It did not save him.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: There is a mountain in Bolivia they call the mountain that eats men.
title: The Mountain That Eats Men
desc:
Potosi's Cerro Rico was full of silver. Under the mita system, Indigenous villages had to send men to work its mines. Many never came home.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: The US dollar was copied from an old Spanish coin.
title: The US Dollar Is a Copy of a Spanish Coin
desc:
The Spanish piece of eight was spent from China to Europe, one of the first global currencies. The American dollar was based on it.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: Spain ruled so much land that the sun never set on it, and its king built a palace with thousands of doors.
title: The Empire Where the Sun Never Set
desc:
Charles V ruled lands around the globe. His son Philip II built El Escorial, a palace and monastery with thousands of doors and windows.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: 130 ships sailed to invade England. Fire and storms sent maybe half of them home.
title: What Really Sank the Spanish Armada
desc:
In 1588 Philip II sent about 130 ships against England. English fire ships broke the formation and storms did the rest.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: Generations of royal cousin marriages ended Spain's greatest dynasty.
title: How Cousin Marriage Ended Spain's Royal Line
desc:
The Spanish Habsburgs married cousins for generations to keep power in the family. The last of them, Charles II, was sickly all his life and had no heir.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

hook: One ship exploded in Havana, and Spain lost an empire 400 years old in a single year.
title: One Explosion Ended a 400-Year Empire
desc:
In February 1898 the USS Maine blew up in Havana harbour. Within months Spain had lost Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.
